paragraphs: Friend, here's what I take from this one. The disciples are admiring stones that look permanent, and Jesus says not one will be left on another (Luke 21:6). Then He gives them a whole list: people claiming, "I am He," wars, earthquakes, famines, persecution (Luke 21:8-12). Notice what He keeps saying in the middle of all that. "See to it that you are not deceived," and "do not be alarmed" (Luke 21:8-9).

Jesus doesn't give them a date. He gives them a way to stand, and I think that's a gift. Wars and rebellions are not the end showing up right away (Luke 21:9), so a loud headline doesn't get to run the bakery. And when the hard days come for them, He calls being dragged before kings "your opportunity to serve as witnesses" (Luke 21:13), and promises "speech and wisdom" (Luke 21:15). I have lost a LOT of arguments I never even had, so I love that He says the words will be given.

So what does that mean for you, baker? Things you trust can fall, and rumors that the end is near can come with a big confident voice, but you don't have to follow them. Jesus says "not even a hair of your head will perish," and "By your patient endurance you will gain your souls" (Luke 21:18-19). That is why my ovens stay ready and my apron stays on. Hold steady, keep your eyes on Jesus, and stay baking.
